title: Love and obedience to parents
intro: After worshipping Allah, the strongest duty is kindness to our parents.

learn.html: Loving and obeying our parents is not a matter of choice. In the Qur’an, right after worshipping Him, Allah made it a strict duty – fard – that in our deeds, words and feelings we obey our parents and show them our love.

learn.title: 📖 In the Qur’an
learn.html: Your Lord has commanded that you worship none but Him, and that you be good to your parents. If one or both of them reach old age with you, do not say to them even “uff”, and do not shout at them, but speak to them with respect. Lower to them the wing of humility out of mercy and say: “My Lord, have mercy on them as they brought me up when I was small.” <small>(Qur’an, Al-Isra 17:23–24)</small>

No better description of how to treat our parents could be given. We are good to them and gentle with them, even when one day we think differently. We take special care with our words and never speak harshly to our mother or father. We show our love when we help them, because we know how much they sacrificed for us. Ibn ‘Umar (RA) explained this ayah: “When you speak to your parents, say: ‘Dear father’, ‘Dear mother’.”

learn.title: A great sin
learn.html: Disobeying parents is a great sin. We may not go against our parents except when they tell us to do a sin. The companions asked the Prophet (SAW) about the best deed, and among the best he named obedience to parents. Kindness to parents is one of the deeds most beloved to Allah.

learn.title: 📖 In the Qur’an
learn.html: If they push you to associate with Me something you have no knowledge of, do not obey them – but keep good company with them in this world, and follow the way of those who turn to Me. <small>(Qur’an, Luqman 31:15)</small>
